stories.title: Rate allotments on a grounds round
stories.statement: I go round the grounds as assessor and give every allotment a one-to-five mark for how well it's worked, with a picture, so that abandoned ones get caught before they go wild.
details: Marks are saved without a connection and upload once there's coverage.
Three or higher requires three-quarters of the area to be growing something.

stories.title: Accept or decline a plot offer
stories.statement: I get an offer when a plot comes free and I'm next in line, and I accept or decline it within fourteen days, so that plots don't sit empty. The offer also names the nearest water tap.
details: The offer shows the plot size, a photo and the annual rent.
If I don't answer in fourteen days, the offer goes to the next person.
Declining twice moves me to the bottom of that list.

stories.title: Split a full plot into halves
stories.statement: I split a full-size plot into two half plots with their own numbers as site coordinator, so that more people on the list can start growing sooner.

stories.title: Donate a tool to the shed
Check a tool back in
stories.statement: I check a tool back in by scanning the QR tag on it, so that the next borrower can see it's back on the hook.
details: If I haven't checked in an hour after my slot ends, the coordinator gets an alert.
Fuel level is recorded for petrol tools.

stories.title: See my plot's water use
stories.statement: I see how many litres my plot used each week this season, taken from its sub-meter, so that I can tell whether mulching is actually saving water.
details: The chart compares my use with the site average for plots of the same size.

stories.title: Tool donations with a wish list
stories.statement: I offer a tool I no longer need to the shared shed, and the coordinator accepts it into the catalogue, so that others can borrow it. I also see a wish list of tools the shed is short of, ranked by how often people asked for them.

stories.title: Join a watering rota and Unpaid rent reminders
stories.statement: I join a watering rota with the neighbours in my row, so that our plots get watered while any of us is away. I get reminders at seven, fourteen and twenty-eight days if my rent is unpaid, so that I sort it out before my tenancy is at risk.
details: Each person picks the days they cover.
I get a reminder the evening before my turn.
I can swap a day with someone else on the rota.
Each reminder has a pay-now link.

stories.title: Check water tank levels
stories.statement: I check how full each water tank on my site is before I walk down, so that I bring cans from home when the tanks are low.
details: Levels come from float sensors and update every thirty minutes.

stories.title: Water use with a seasonal allowance
stories.statement: I see how many litres my plot used each week this season, taken from its sub-meter, so that I can tell whether mulching is actually saving water. I also get a seasonal water allowance for my plot and see how much of it is left.
details: The chart compares my use with the site average for plots of the same size.
The allowance scales with plot size.

stories.title: Post surplus produce
details: Posts expire after three days.
I can mark a post as gone.

stories.title: Borrow from the seed library
stories.statement: I borrow seed packets from the site seed library and return saved seed from my own crop at the end of the season, so that the library keeps itself stocked.
details: Each variety shows germination notes from past borrowers.
I can take up to five packets at a time.

stories.title: Book a green waste skip slot
stories.statement: I book a slot to tip woody prunings in the green waste skip, so that the skip isn't overfilled before collection day.
details: Each slot is 20 minutes and covers one car boot or wheelbarrow load.
Slots close when the skip is marked three-quarters full.

stories.title: Track my volunteer hours
stories.statement: I see my volunteer hours for the year against the twelve hours every plot holder owes, so that I know if I'm short before renewal. A reminder comes a month before renewal.
details: Hours are added when the organiser marks attendance after a work party.

stories.title: Suggest a work party job and Report rats at the compost
stories.statement: I suggest a job for the next work party, like clearing the bramble corner, so that jobs nobody owns get done. I report rats near the compost bays, so that pest control is called.
details: Other holders can upvote suggestions.
The organiser picks from the top five when planning.
Three reports in a week trigger an automatic call-out request.

stories.title: Sign up for a work party
stories.statement: I sign up for a Saturday work party and pick a task such as hedge cutting or path weeding, so that the organiser knows how many people to expect.
details: Each task has a cap on helpers.
I can cancel up to the evening before.

stories.title: Pay annual plot rent
stories.statement: I pay my yearly plot rent by card in the app, so that I don't have to post a cheque to the council.
details: Rent is due on 1 October and the app shows the amount from September.

stories.title: Apply for a concession rate
stories.statement: I apply for the half-price concession by uploading proof of pension or benefits, so that I pay what I can afford.
details: The treasurer approves or rejects each application.
Approval lasts one year and must be renewed.

stories.title: Volunteer hours shared across a joint tenancy
stories.statement: I see my volunteer hours for the year against the twelve hours every plot holder owes, so that I know if I'm short before renewal. I also pool hours with my joint tenant, so either of us can cover the other's share.
details: Hours are added when the organiser marks attendance after a work party.

stories.title: Pay a refundable plot deposit
stories.statement: I pay a refundable £50 deposit when my tenancy starts and get it back when I leave the plot in good order, so that clearing abandoned plots isn't paid for by everyone.
details: The deposit is held separately from rent in the accounts.
The coordinator records the exit check that releases it.

stories.title: Renew by direct debit
stories.statement: I set up a direct debit so my rent renews each October without me doing anything, so that I never lose my plot over a missed payment.
details: The mandate is collected on 1 October.
I'm warned by email ten days before each collection.

stories.title: Upload concession proof
stories.statement: I upload a photo of my pension or benefits letter from my phone, so that the treasurer can check my concession.
details: The upload takes a photo or a PDF.

stories.title: Settle the allotment fee online
stories.statement: I clear the annual charge for my allotment online from my phone, so that I'm not mailing paper payments to the local authority. I also get the receipt by email.
details: The charge falls due each October the first and appears from the start of September.

stories.title: Record a plot inspection
stories.statement: I walk the site as inspector and score each plot on cultivation from 1 to 5 with a photo, so that neglected plots are spotted early.
details: Scores work offline and sync when I'm back in signal.
A plot needs at least 75% cultivated to score 3 or more.

stories.title: Request the reduced fee
stories.statement: I send in evidence of retirement income or welfare support and ask for the 50% discount, so that the cost stays within my means.
details: Each request is signed off or turned down by the committee's finance officer.
A granted discount runs for twelve months, then I reapply.
